## Summary

Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDatePrinterAgentTest.java` with 50 self-contained JUnit 5 tests covering formatting (dates, calendars, longs), time-zone handling (`Z`/`ZZ`/`ZZZ`, `X`/`XX`/`XXX` ISO 8601 rules), hour-field midnight boundaries, year-pattern quirks, day-of-week/day-of-year numeric fields, quoting/escaping, `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`, serialization, `getMaxLengthEstimate`, and various error paths.

48 tests pass. 2 fail, and both point to a real bug:

- **`testConstructorNullTimeZoneThrowsNullPointerExceptionPerJavadoc`** — `FastDatePrinter`'s constructor javadoc states `@throws NullPointerException if pattern, timeZone, or locale is null`, but passing a `null` `TimeZone` with a pattern that doesn't contain `z`/`Z` tokens (e.g. `"yyyy-MM-dd"`) silently succeeds; the `null` is stored unchecked and only surfaces as an NPE later when something actually dereferences the zone.
- **`testConstructorNullLocaleThrowsNullPointerExceptionPerJavadoc`** — same javadoc contract, but `LocaleUtils.toLocale(null)` quietly substitutes `Locale.getDefault()` instead of throwing, so a `null` locale is silently replaced rather than rejected.
